title: Tachikawa air disaster
summary: A United States Air Force Douglas C-124A Globemaster II crashed on June 18, 1953, three minutes after takeoff from Tachikawa Air Base, Japan. The aircraft's No. 1 outer left engine burst into flames one minute into the flight. The commander shut down the engine and declared return to base, requesting ground-controlled approach. However, during return procedures the left wing stalled, causing the aircraft to roll left into an unrecoverable dive. The aircraft crashed into a watermelon patch 3.5 miles from the airbase, killing all 129 people aboard. The investigation determined the crash was caused by improper flap usage and airspeed loss following the port engine failure.
probable_cause: Improper flap usage and airspeed loss due to the failure of the port engine, resulting in wing stall and loss of control.

title: Transocean Air Lines 512
summary: Transocean Air Lines Flight 512, a Douglas DC-6A, disappeared over the Pacific Ocean approximately 630 kilometers east of Wake Island while en route to Honolulu. The aircraft had departed Wake Island at 06:58 GMT and missed its next scheduled position report. Another aircraft flying north of the scheduled route reported encountering an extensive thunderstorm with heavy turbulence, though the pre-departure weather briefing did not indicate significant turbulence. The fuselage was not recovered, preventing mechanical analysis.
probable_cause: Unable to determine; fuselage not recovered and no physical evidence of fire or mechanical failure could be examined.
